"Implement the solution in queen_attack.cpp, queen_attack.h so that the tests in queen_attack_test.cpp pass. The specification follows.

# Instructions

Given the position of two queens on a chess board, indicate whether or not they are positioned so that they can attack each other.

In the game of chess, a queen can attack pieces which are on the same row, column, or diagonal.

A chessboard can be represented by an 8 by 8 array.

So if you are told the white queen is at `c5` (zero-indexed at column 2, row 3) and the black queen at `f2` (zero-indexed at column 5, row 6), then you know that the set-up is like so:

![A chess board with two queens. Arrows emanating from the queen at c5 indicate possible directions of capture along file, rank and diagonal.](https://assets.exercism.org/images/exercises/queen-attack/queen-capture.svg)

You are also able to answer whether the queens can attack each other.
In this case, that answer would be yes, they can, because both pieces share a diagonal.

## Credit

The chessboard image was made by [habere-et-dispertire][habere-et-dispertire] using LaTeX and the [chessboard package][chessboard-package] by Ulrike Fischer.

[habere-et-dispertire]: https://exercism.org/profiles/habere-et-dispertire
[chessboard-package]: https://github.com/u-fischer/chessboard


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper .h / .cpp files may go beside the solution."

I'll just summarize the solution.

The implementation is complete. Here's what I did:

## Solution

**`queen_attack.h`** — Declares a `chess_board` class in the `queen_attack` namespace:
- Constructor taking `std::pair<int, int>` positions for white and black queens (pair is `{column, row}`)
- `white()` / `black()` accessors returning the stored positions
- `can_attack()` returning whether the queens share a row, column, or diagonal
- A private `validate_position()` helper

**`queen_attack.cpp`** — Implementation:
- **Validation**: throws `std::domain_error` if either queen's column or row is outside `0..7`, and if both queens occupy the same square
- **`can_attack()`**: returns `true` if the queens share a column (`first` equal) or row (`second` equal), or if `|col_diff| == |row_diff|` (same diagonal)

## Test results

The build succeeded with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`, and the test binary ran clean:

```
All tests passed (2 assertions in 1 test case)
```

Note: by default the suite only runs the first test case; the remaining 12 cases (validation errors, all diagonal/row/column attack scenarios) are gated behind `EXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS`. My implementation covers all of them — positions are validated in the constructor before storage, and the diagonal check uses absolute column/row differences, which handles all four diagonal directions including the "reflected across the longest falling diagonal" negative case.

I attempted to re-run the full suite with `EXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS=ON`, but the commands were declined — if you'd like, you can verify with:

```
cmake -S . -B build -DEXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS=ON && cmake --build build && ./build/queen-attack
```
